definitions.explanation: A T-shaped wooden stand hung with silk panels, used in Heian-period aristocratic houses to divide a room and to shield noblewomen from view. It appears constantly in classical literature and in period drama sets.

examples.japanese: {几帳|きちょう}の{陰|かげ}に{隠|かく}れる。
examples.english: She hides behind the standing screen.

examples.japanese: {部屋|へや}の{中|なか}を{几帳|きちょう}で{仕切|しき}っていた。
examples.english: The room was partitioned with curtained screens.

examples.japanese: {平安|へいあん}{時代|じだい}の{女性|じょせい}は{几帳|きちょう}{越|ご}しに{客|きゃく}と{話|はな}すのが{普通|ふつう}だった。
examples.english: Heian-period women normally spoke with visitors from the other side of a curtained screen.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {几帳|きちょう}{越|ご}しに{話|はな}す: to speak through a screen
- {几帳|きちょう}を{立|た}てる: to set up a screen
- {几帳|きちょう}の{陰|かげ}: behind the screen

RELATED WORDS:
The adjective {几帳面|きちょうめん} (methodical, meticulous) is said to derive from the precise decorative joinery of the {几帳}'s posts — a useful memory hook, since the two words look related but describe very different things.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {屏風|びょうぶ}: folding screen — rigid, hinged panels rather than hanging cloth
- {襖|ふすま}: sliding door panel — a fixed part of the building, not portable
